item.title: skroutz-cli: built for personal assistants
item.description:
A CLI for skroutz.gr that logs into my real account over OAuth and calls the exact MCP server Skroutz built for its ChatGPT and Claude connectors: 27 tools, no schemas parked in your context.
[skroutz-cli](https://github.com/glogiotatidis/skroutz-cli) is a terminal client for [Skroutz](https://www.skroutz.gr). It logs in with OAuth 2.1 (dynamic client registration, PKCE, one scope, `shopping_mcp`) and then talks to the same MCP server Skroutz shipped for its ChatGPT and Claude connectors: `https://api.skroutz.gr/api/agents/mcp/shopping`, JSON-RPC 2.0 over streamable HTTP, protocol 2025-06-18. 27 tools: search, cart, orders, addresses, returns.
Two earlier attempts are gone from the code now. First, scraping the storefront with [curl_cffi](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi) to fake a Chrome TLS fingerprint past Cloudflare. Then replaying browser session cookies to drive a cart, which got far enough to place a real order and cancel it just to prove the path worked. Both deleted once the MCP door turned out to be unlocked.
> A connector is a tax on every conversation. A CLI is a tool you pick up.
A connector hands your agent all 27 tool schemas before it knows it needs any of them, every single conversation. A CLI is a capability you pick up when you need it and put down again, which is why it suits a harness more than a chat window. That is true of [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/), [openclaw](https://github.com/openclaw), [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), or anything else that can open a shell. [Anthropic measured the same shape](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp): agents writing code against MCP servers instead of loading their schemas dropped from 150,000 tokens to 2,000.
**MCP is the wire. A CLI is the handle you actually turn.**
Finding the wire was the actual work. The endpoint is in no directory I could query, and about ninety guessed paths 404'd before I gave up guessing. I exported a HAR of my own Claude session with the connector page open, and the URL was sitting right there in the browser traffic. Once I had it, Hermes running DeepSeek flash wrote the whole client in one night while I slept: 1,400 lines of Python, 33 tests.
The OAuth endpoints and the MCP server both answer plain HTTP, so the CLI has zero runtime dependencies, stdlib only. Two honest limits: search returns at most 10 results per call, and the price you get is `cart_price` (plus `lowest_price`), the number Skroutz's own cart would charge you. There is no per-shop offer list on the MCP side, so don't expect this to compare sellers.
See also: - Source on GitHub — https://github.com/glogiotatidis/skroutz-cli - Anthropic on code execution with MCP — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp - Model Context Protocol — https://modelcontextprotocol.io/

item.title: Greek TV Streamio: Greek on-demand TV in Stremio
item.description:
Greek stations publish their shows on six different webtv sites with no shared catalog. This addon scrapes all of them, resolves every episode to a direct stream, and serves it to Stremio and Nuvio as static JSON.
Six stations, six webtv sites, no shared catalog: Skai hides the episode list in a JSON blob inside the page, ERT has a real API, the rest are somewhere in between. So I wrote one adapter per station and a [Stremio](https://www.stremio.com/) addon on top.
It currently exports **385 shows and 20,019 episodes**. It answers the three protocol calls, catalog, meta and stream, and every episode resolves to a direct MP4 or HLS URL.
There is no server. A static export writes it all as JSON under `catalog/`, `meta/` and `stream/`, and [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) publishes that straight to GitHub Pages: 20,414 files, 10.2 MiB. Every four hours it runs one job per station, with `fail-fast` off so a station that breaks does not take the others down, then merges the artifacts. A normal run reuses the previous show list and stream URLs, so only new episodes cost a request.
Requests go through [curl_cffi](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi) with a Chrome TLS fingerprint, and the helper honours `Retry-After` on a 429. A daily smoke test resolves a stream, follows the redirect and pulls one segment, which is how I find out a station redesigned its site before a viewer does. Nineteen of those 20,019 episodes come back empty. The rest resolve.
Add the [manifest](https://glogiotatidis.github.io/greektv-streamio/manifest.json) to Stremio and the shows are there, by station or all together.
See also: - Install the manifest — https://glogiotatidis.github.io/greektv-streamio/manifest.json - Source on GitHub — https://github.com/glogiotatidis/greektv-streamio

item.title: A place for the things I build
item.description:
I'm starting a small timeline to post the things I build, as I build them. Short entries, links, snippets. No comments, no analytics.
I've wanted a place to drop the things I build as I build them. Not a full blog post every time, just a short entry with a link and maybe a snippet. So here it is: a small timeline.
It's a plain static site, no framework, no runtime build. Posts are Markdown files with a bit of frontmatter; a Python script compiles them into the JSON the page reads. No build to break. Adding an entry is a new file and one command.
If you want to follow along, there's an RSS feed.
